title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; study_id cnd-001-5f3a) to evaluate whether a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that applies a deterministic validator and at most one deterministic rule-based repair to a single shared LLM candidate improves emulator-executable success relative to ungated LLM generation. Generation used gpt-5-mini with one shared candidate per intent; the guarded arm applied a three-stage deterministic validator and a deterministic repair operator when eligibility rules were met. Artifact-backed primary outcomes: baseline = 199/200 (0.995), guarded = 200/200 (1.000); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact binomial on discordant pairs) yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target is excluded because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. We report concise algorithmic descriptions of the deterministic validator and repair operator, execution accounting (hosted-model calls used = 201; repair invocations = 1), representative exemplars and difficulty context, exact-test justification for small discordant counts, operational interpretation, and artifact-backed limitations. All prompts, provider traces, validator and repair traces, and analysis artifacts are archived in the study evidence bundle.

sections.introduction: Automating routine network-operations changes with large language models (LLMs) promises operational efficiency but raises safety and correctness concerns: syntactic errors, missing required steps, dependency/order violations, and protected-field modifications. Prior work proposes mitigations—retrieval-augmented generation, constrained decoding, verifier-assisted loops, and tool-augmented repair—but empirical, execution-grounded quantification of modest, low-cost repair policies remains limited. We study the marginal yield of a bounded, deterministic repair operator applied to the same initial LLM candidate (shared-initial-generation estimand). This estimand is operationally relevant when teams minimize model-call budgets (one hosted-model call per intent). Our preregistered research question: Does an iterative generate–verify–repair pipeline that pairs hosted-LLM generation with deterministic verification and a bounded deterministic repair (≤1 iteration) yield a higher emulator-executable configuration success rate than ungated LLM generation when both arms evaluate the same initial candidate? Contributions: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation under the shared-candidate estimand; (2) concise algorithmic descriptions of the deterministic validator (3-stage) and the deterministic repair operator (insertion/reordering/preservation enforcement); (3) exact-test justification and artifact-grounded execution accounting; and (4) a frank operational interpretation and limitations grounded in the archived run.
sections.related_work: Recent literature documents active application of LLMs to intent-to-configuration translation, co-pilot assistance, and prototype NetOps systems while reporting structured-output failure modes. Surveys and prototypes (intent-based translation, co-pilots, AIOps integrations) show promise but often stop short of end-to-end execution grounding under deterministic verification. Cross-domain mitigation methods (RAG, live schema grounding, constrained decoding) effectively reduce hallucinations in NL2SQL and document-grounded tasks; verifier-assisted repair and multi-stage architectures have demonstrable benefit in adjacent domains but are under-evaluated specifically for device-CLI configuration generation. Formal verification methods (NetKAT variants, weighted NetKAT and ensemble verifiers) provide deterministic checks for reachability and policy conformance but require accurate control-plane state to be meaningful. Agentic NetOps architecture literature stresses surrounding assurance machinery (evidence traces, bounded tool use, rollback policies) as necessary for operational reliability. Our study occupies the intersection of these lines: we evaluate a lightweight, deterministic GVR pipeline that is low in model-call cost and auditable via archived validator and repair traces. Representative verified sources that informed design and interpretation include Nguyen et al. (intent-based network configuration), formal NetKAT variants [doi:10.1145/3808318], and recent surveys/architectural treatments of LLM NetOps [https://openalex.org/W7161165783].
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design: The confirmatory protocol (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) prespecified a paired, shared-initial-generation design over n=200 curated natural-language intents. For each intent a hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini) produced a single initial candidate; that candidate was scored both as the baseline (ungated acceptance) and, after deterministic validation and eligible repair, as the guarded result. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Primary test: exact two-sided McNemar implemented via the exact binomial formulation on discordant counts (see Statistical Procedures). Planned maximum hosted-model calls = 400; realized model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair-stage calls = 1). Confirmatory execution used Dockerized Mininet + FRR routers orchestrated by adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and a deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5.

Task bank, inclusion rules, and scoring: The confirmatory bank contains 200 curated intent–reference pairs targeting single-device and small multi-device changes (VLAN, MTU, uplink switchover, safe-sequence policies). Inclusion rules and contamination checks were preregistered; no confirmatory pair was excluded. Scoring applied a full_intent_constraint_validation rule: a candidate must (a) syntactically parse into canonical CLI tokens, (b) include the task’s required_sequence, (c) satisfy dependency/group policies (make-before-break, shutdown_configure_restore, minimum-active constraints), (d) avoid protected-interface modifications, and (e) produce an emulator observed_final_state matching the expected_final_state. Episodes with provider/API generation errors would be scored as failures per preregistration; none occurred.

Deterministic validator (concise technical description): The validator deterministically executes three ordered stages and emits a structured trace used for scoring and repair decisions. Stage 1—syntactic parse and canonical normalization—tokenizes CLI-like lines and produces normalized_configuration or flags SYNTAX_PARSE_ERROR. Stage 2—structural/workflow checks—verifies presence of required commands, ordering/dependency constraints, group-activity and protected-interface policies; each detected issue is assigned a deterministic violation code (e.g., MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND, DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_MODIFICATION). Stage 3—deterministic emulator application—applies the normalized configuration to the emulator to obtain observed_final_state and compares it against the task’s expected_final_state. The boolean validation outcome used for primary scoring is validation_after.valid. Validator traces archive parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count and the canonical normalized_configuration for every episode.

Deterministic repair operator (concise algorithmic description): The repair operator is a deterministic, rule-based transformation invoked only when the validator reports violation_count > 0 and the violation family belongs to a preregistered repairable set. Operational constraints enforced by the preregistration: (1) no additional LLM calls—repairs are deterministic code transformations; (2) bounded budget—at most one repair per episode (repair_budget ≤ 1); (3) unambiguous mapping—repairs apply only when the mapping from violation code to a single deterministic transformation is unambiguous. The operator implements three canonical deterministic transformations: (i) Insertion: insert missing required commands derived from the task’s required_sequence (e.g., insert shutdown/restore steps when shutdown_configure_restore is required); (ii) Reordering: atomically reorder annotated command blocks to satisfy dependency constraints while preserving syntactic group boundaries; (iii) Preservation enforcement: redact or deterministically rewrite commands that would violate preserve_unspecified_state or protected-interface policies by reinstating original values from the task initial_state. Ambiguous violations (e.g., multiple plausible insertion points) are not repaired and remain failures. All repair decisions and resulting normalized_configuration are recorded in an archived repair trace; the run invoked the repair operator exactly once (repair invocations = 1). The repair trace and provider-call audit showing repair-stage usage are archived in the execution bundle for audit.

Statistical procedures and preregistered analyses: Primary hypothesis H1 used McNemar’s paired binary test in its exact binomial form suitable for small discordant totals. Define n10 = count(guarded=1, baseline=0) and n01 = count(guarded=0, baseline=1); the number of discordants n = n10 + n01. Under the null the count of observed n10 (or n01) follows Binomial(n, 0.5), and the two-sided p-value is computed from the exact binomial tail probabilities. Complementary uncertainty quantification used paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CIs with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). The preregistered power calculation targeted an absolute effect = 0.15 at n=200 assuming baseline ≈0.50; the realized near-ceiling baseline reduces attainable discordants and thus inferential sensitivity. Secondary, exploratory analyses (predeclared) include repair_iteration counts and failure-taxonomy summaries; these are reported descriptively.
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcomes: The run executed all planned episodes (400 episodes = 200 pairs) without provider/API generation failures. Artifact-backed primary counts: baseline_success_count = 199/200 (0.995) and guarded_success_count = 200/200 (1.0). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0, giving paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Applying the preregistered exact McNemar two-sided test (exact-binomial on discordant pairs with n = 1, observed n10 = 1, n01 = 0) yields two-sided p = 1.0: with a single discordant observation the two-sided binomial tail probability equals 1.0 under p = 0.5 because the two-sided test aggregates both tails for n = 1 symmetric cases. The paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) percentile 95% CI for the paired difference is [0.0, 0.015]. All per-episode JSONL scoring artifacts and analysis results are archived.

Repair and failure accounting: validation_before.valid was false in exactly one confirmatory episode; deterministic repair invocations = 1, and that single deterministic repair transformed the failing candidate into a validator-passing configuration, producing the sole guarded-only success (n10 = 1). Syntactic/parse failures across the confirmatory set = 0. Missingness summary: no missing or unscorable episodes. Provider-call audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, cache_miss_count = 201, stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 200, repair = 1.

Representative exemplars, difficulty context, and task coverage: To aid interpretation we archived six representative exemplars (manifested among execution/task_manifest.jsonl). The six exemplars carry difficulty labels medium = 1, hard = 2, very_hard = 3; these exemplars illustrate dependency and workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break, paired MTU changes, safe access transfer). The full per-episode difficulty metadata for all 200 confirmatory intents is archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl in the evidence bundle for readers who require the complete distribution. The curated confirmatory bank intentionally focuses on single-device and small multi-device changes; it does not represent broad production heterogeneity of multivendor CLIs or long-lived control-plane dynamics.

Sensitivity, power, and interpretive statistics: The preregistered detectable absolute effect (0.15) assumed baseline ≈0.50; with observed baseline ≈0.995 the number of potential discordant pairs is constrained and the study lacks power to detect large absolute improvements from a near-ceiling baseline. The observed two-sided exact p = 1.0 indicates no departure from the null under the exact-binomial McNemar given the observed discordance pattern. The bootstrap CI excludes a 0.15 absolute improvement, so the preregistered substantial-effect target is not supported by the data. Practically, deterministic repair-on-same-candidate produced a single marginal improvement in this curated distribution.

Execution accounting summary (artifact-backed): completed_episodes = 400; model_calls_used = 201; shared_initial_generation calls = 200; repair-stage calls = 1; failed_hosted_model_calls = 0. Analysis artifacts (paired contingency CSV, condition summary, missingness and contamination reports) are archived and referenced in the evidence bundle.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation: Under the shared-initial-generation estimand and the curated confirmatory distribution, ungated gpt-5-mini generation produced near-perfect candidates (199/200) and the bounded deterministic repair produced one additional pass. Two practical points follow: (1) deterministic validators provide structured violation codes that enable auditable, low-cost deterministic repair; (2) when base-model generation is near-ceiling for the target distribution, conservative rule-based repairs applied to the same candidate yield limited marginal improvement while preserving low model-call cost.

Design-space trade-offs and estimand choice: The shared-candidate estimand intentionally minimises model-call cost (one generation per intent). Alternative operational architectures—independent-resampling (separate LLM draws per arm), multi-iteration LLM-invoked repair, or increased deterministic repair budgets—could increase success rates but at higher hosted-model cost and governance complexity. Our execution accounting (model_calls_used = 201; repair invocations = 1) enables simple cost–yield comparisons for practitioners deciding between low-cost guarded designs and higher-cost multi-resample strategies.

Threats to validity: Internal validity is strong for the paired estimand and deterministic scoring rules; construct validity depends on whether the deterministic emulator and validator adequately represent operational risks (they deterministically model control-plane effects but do not capture some timing-dependent runtime dynamics). External validity is limited by the single LLM evaluated (gpt-5-mini), the curated confirmatory bank, and the Dockerized emulator's fidelity to heterogeneous vendor hardware. Conclusion validity is constrained by the near-ceiling baseline, which limits discordant counts and inferential sensitivity. These threats and their measured impact are documented in the preregistration and archived manifests.

Implications and next steps: Deterministic validators are essential assurance machinery for auditable NetOps pipelines. When operational budgets constrain model calls, a shared-candidate guarded design with deterministic validation may be attractive; where maximal success is paramount, independent-resampling or LLM-invoked multi-step repair designs should be evaluated. Future artifact-backed work should compare estimands (shared-candidate vs independent-resampling), expand multivendor CLI coverage, include adversarial and out-of-distribution intents, and evaluate larger or LLM-guided repair budgets and higher-fidelity control-plane dynamics.
sections.conclusion: We executed an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment evaluating a bounded generate–verify–repair guard on gpt-5-mini outputs under a shared-initial-generation estimand. Ungated generation succeeded in 199/200 confirmatory cases; the GVR pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 deterministic repair) succeeded in 200/200. Observed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]) and does not support the preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. For this estimand and curated distribution, deterministic repair-on-same-candidate produced negligible marginal gain. Deterministic validators remain operationally valuable as auditable assurance gates; choosing estimands and repair budgets aligned to operational goals is critical. All study artifacts, traces, and analysis code are archived in the evidence bundle for independent audit and re-analysis.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock. The initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt and autonomy boundary. No manual human editing of technical content, results, figures, captions, references, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. Models and tooling: generation requested gpt-5-mini via the hosted-model provider recorded in the execution manifest; deterministic validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (stages: syntactic parse + normalization; structural/workflow checks; deterministic emulator application); the deterministic repair operator is rule-based and invoked without additional LLM calls. Execution environment: Dockerized Mininet + FRR images orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistered and enforced settings (not altered post-lock): primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample = n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; primary analysis = exact McNemar two-sided (exact-binomial on discordant pairs); paired-bootstrap CIs with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Execution accounting (artifact-backed): completed_episodes = 400; model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair-stage calls = 1). All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair), analysis artifacts, and the execution manifest are archived in the study evidence bundle and referenced in the manuscript.
limitations: Synthetic, curated confirmatory task bank focused on small single- and multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLI dialects, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.

Deterministic emulator + validator model control-plane behavior deterministically but cannot fully capture real-world runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.
Shared-initial-generation design reduces model-call cost and isolates repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness but reduces external generalizability compared with independent-resampling estimands.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

Full per-task difficulty label counts for all 200 confirmatory intents are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl in the evidence bundle rather than enumerated inline here to preserve concise manuscript presentation while preserving auditable reproducibility.
